title: Minimum Platforms Required
statement:
A railway (or bus) station receives `n` trains in one day. Train `i` arrives at time `arrival[i]` and leaves at time `departure[i]`, with `arrival[i] ≤ departure[i]`. A train occupies one platform for the whole closed interval from its arrival time to its departure time, **both endpoints included**.

Two trains cannot share a platform if their intervals share even a single time unit. In particular, if one train departs at exactly the time another arrives, they need different platforms.

Find the minimum number of platforms needed so that every train gets a platform for its entire stay.

Times are plain integers (for example `930` for 9:30 in HHMM form works, but any integers are allowed); only their order matters.
input_format:
The first line contains `n`.
The second line contains `n` integers `arrival[0..n-1]`.
The third line contains `n` integers `departure[0..n-1]`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the minimum number of platforms.

examples.explanation: Between times 810 and 830 the trains [800,900], [805,830] and [810,1000] are all in the station together. No moment has 4 trains.
The first train leaves at 200 and the second arrives at 200. Since both endpoints count, they overlap at time 200 and need separate platforms.
Each train stays for a single instant and the instants are all different, so one platform is enough.

hints: The answer is the largest number of trains present at the same moment. That maximum can only change when a train arrives.
Sort arrivals and departures separately. Sweep through them in time order: an arrival adds one train, a departure removes one.
Decide what happens on ties: an arrival at time t must be processed before a departure at time t, because both trains are present at t.
reference:
import sys


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    arr = sorted(int(x) for x in data[1:1 + n])
    dep = sorted(int(x) for x in data[1 + n:1 + 2 * n])
    i = j = cur = best = 0
    while i < n:
        if arr[i] <= dep[j]:
            cur += 1
            i += 1
            if cur > best:
                best = cur
        else:
            cur -= 1
            j += 1
    print(best)


main()
